processing_steps.method: air induction melting with protective flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.cooling_medium: top poured into split cast iron molds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 30-kg heats using an Inductotherm medium-frequency AIM furnace of 50-kg capacity; commercial purity aluminum and iron; iron charge pickled in dilute hydrochloric acid and charged into an alumina-lined crucible; preheated flux (Al2O3, CaO, MgO, CaF2) added after melting the iron; cleaned and preheated aluminum pieces plunged into the molten iron bath; bath held at 1900 K for 2 min to prevent aluminum losses.
80-mm-diameter AIMFC ingots preheated before hot forging.

processing_steps.method: hot forging in 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 24-mm-thick sections of the forged billets were preheated before hot rolling.
1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes under conditions similar to preheating; final hot-rolled plate thickness 12 mm.

structures.overall_structure: annealed microstructure with coarse grain size

defects.type: residual porosity / second-phase particles (dark rounded dots)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Hardness data point = average of five measurements; tensile data point = average of three tests.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Room-temperature tensile ductility of Fe-7Al produced by AIMFC is comparable to the alloy produced by VIM.
Fe-7Al produced by AIMFC exhibited superior properties compared with the alloy produced by the AIM process; AIM Fe-7Al showed poor room-temperature tensile ductility.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Coarse, equiaxed, fully recrystallised grains with annealing twins; dark rounded dots (residual porosity/second-phase particles) densely decorating grains and boundaries; grain size 195 μm.

characterization_methods.technique: chemical composition analysis; hydrogen analysis by RH-444 Leco Gas analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine chemical composition of the AIMFC ingot

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; each data point average of three tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure UTS, YS, and total elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS 467 ± 5.7 MPa, YS 396 ± 8.1 MPa, EL total 18 ± 1.6%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; each data point average of five measurements

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the Fe-7Al AIMFC ingot (Table I): Al 7.30, Si 0.14, Mn 0.045, S 0.0016, C 0.019, O 0.0057, H 0.0023, N 0.0018 wt.% (hydrogen analyzed by RH-444 Leco Gas analyzer). [b0035, b0036, figure_unlabelled_001]
Aluminum recovery during AIMFC was 95–98%, comparable to VIM (96–98%), and much better than AIM. [b0025]
AIMFC ingots exhibited low sulfur (0.0016 wt.%) attributed to desulfurization by CaO in the flux, and low oxygen (0.0057 wt.%) comparable with VIM ingots. [b0026, b0038]
The Fe-7Al AIMFC ingots were sound, porosity-free, and completely free from microcracks (in contrast to Fe-9Al AIMFC ingots, which exhibited microcracks). [b0023, b0024]

Fe-7Al produced by AIMFC could be further cold rolled to thin sheets and foils (Fig. 3); a cold-rolled and annealed 2-mm sheet exhibited UTS 467 ± 5.8 MPa, YS 340 ± 8.1 MPa, and total elongation 40 ± 3.5% (Table III). [b0041, b0042, b0046, b0047, figure_unlabelled_002]

The room-temperature tensile ductility of Fe-7Al AIMFC was comparable to VIM, while AIM Fe-7Al showed poor ductility attributed to hydrogen embrittlement and higher O/S nonmetallic inclusions. [b0042]
Hot-rolled Fe-7Al AIMFC exhibited excellent hot workability (as did all Fe-7Al melting routes). [b0041]
